title: The Hop Goblins job and forming his own band
summary: Parker tells of managing the Lions Band, a Halloween job for the Goblins, and making up a band the year of the big storm.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yes. The first band, yeah, the Lions Band, oh yeah. The Lions Band. Lions, right across the street there. Mm-hmm. I was the manager of the Lions Band, right across the street there. Mm-hmm.
I was the manager of the Lions Band, right across the street there. Mm-hmm .
You see, I got a job out of the management of the band. I was in the Hop Goblins band. They had a band called the Hop Goblins. On Halloween night, it was a big night for the Goblins, you know?

So, I get a job, $90, for liberty. And he arrived right now. He wasn't born then. He lived. Wasn't thought of. And I get this job and I pick out 11 men beside myself. 12 men to play that $90 job, you know? We had 35 men in the Garbage van, you know? So, the fellas I didn't pick out, they got committed, Captain Jones, and brought them to my house on a Friday. We went down there on the Central Rock Street. So, Captain Jones called me and said, well, Paola, I'll tell you all that job left for the first. I said, yes, it is. He said, well, did you take that job on the Goblins man? I said, I did. He said, well, I'll tell you, Paola. If you take that job on, on and back and then, every man in the Goblins man got to play that job. I said, you're right, Captain. Captain Jones is in here on time. But my nephew, back there, was the first bass drummer. He wouldn't, he didn't want to play. And that made me have to take it, you know. So I took the beat of Saratoga. Went on to replace that job.
